✦ Workspace Assistant Swift guide

Tutorial

Build an On-Device AI Agent

Build Workspace Assistant: a task board that an AI agent changes for you while you watch. You'll model the board, draw it in SwiftUI, give Apple's Foundation Models framework tools to call, and let the user and the agent work side by side. Everything runs on the device.

New to some of the Swift? Keep the Swift Code Guide open as you go: it explains every keyword and attribute these tutorials use, such as @Observable, private(set), @MainActor and @Generable.

Swift Code Guide

Every keyword and @ attribute you meet in the WorkspaceAssistant tutorials, explained with the app's own code. Examples come from WorkspaceAssistant Lite; a few items marked Full only appear only in the Full version. In Full, the same keywords appear in different files: WorkspaceStore, the view models and the services.

Most of these appear together in one place. The top of Workspace.swift reads like this:

@MainActor               // all of its code runs on the main thread, like the UI@Observable              // SwiftUI redraws any view that reads a property when it changesfinal class Workspace {  // a class (shared, by reference) that nothing may subclass    var tasks: [TaskItem] = TaskItem.samples    private(set) var actions: [AgentAction] = []   // anyone can read it; only Workspace can change it}

The table is the quick index. The sections below explain each item.

Types: struct, class, enum, protocol, extension

The app uses struct for data, final class for the two shared objects that change over time, and enum for fixed choices.

struct: a value you copy

struct TaskItem: Identifiable, Hashable {    let id = UUID()    var title: String    var isDone = false}

Assigning a struct makes an independent copy, so changing the copy never changes the original. That makes data predictable, and it's why TaskItem, AgentAction and every tool are structs. let properties never change after creation; var properties can.

SwiftUI views are structs too (struct ContentView: View). They're cheap descriptions of the screen, rebuilt whenever data changes.

class and final class: one shared object

final class Workspace { … }final class TaskAgent { … }

A class is a reference type: everyone who holds a Workspace holds the same one. The board, the agent's tools and the new-task sheet must all change the same tasks, so Workspace is a class.

final means no other class can inherit from it. It documents that subclassing isn't planned, and lets the compiler call methods a little faster. In app code, make classes final unless you have a reason not to.

enum: a fixed set of choices

enum BoardLayout: String, CaseIterable {    case grid, list, board}

A BoardLayout can only be one of those three values, so a typo can't create a fourth. : String gives each case a rawValue ("grid"), and CaseIterable provides BoardLayout.allCases, which the layout picker loops over. Enums can also carry code, like the symbol property each layout uses for its icon.

Enums with no cases can't be created at all. SimulatedAgent is written as an enum on purpose: it's just a namespace for static functions.

protocol and conformance: promises a type keeps

The names after the colon are protocols the type promises to satisfy:

ProtocolPromiseWhy the app needs it
IdentifiableHas an idForEach(workspace.orderedTasks) can tell tasks apart and animate them
HashableCan be compared and hashed.animation(value: workspace.tasks) detects changes
CaseIterableLists all its casesForEach(BoardLayout.allCases, …) in the picker
ToolHas name, description, Arguments, callThe model can call it
ViewHas a bodySwiftUI can draw it
AppHas a body that returns a SceneIt can be the app's entry point

Swift writes the code for Hashable and CaseIterable automatically when every property allows it. In the Full version, TaskRepository is the app's own protocol, so SwiftData and in-memory storage can be swapped (Full only).

extension: more code for an existing type

extension TaskItem {    static let samples: [TaskItem] = [ … ]}

An extension adds properties or functions to a type, even one you didn't write. The app uses them to keep sample data and display code (icons, colours) out of the main type.

static: belongs to the type

TaskItem.samples is written on the type, not on one task, because there's one list of samples for the whole app. Inside the type you can write Self.samples. TaskAgent.makeSession is static because it builds a session before the agent itself exists.

Access control: who may see and change what

Access control keeps the rule "only Workspace changes the board" true: other code can read its state, but must go through its methods to change it.

final class TaskAgent {    let workspace: Workspace                  // anyone can read; nobody can replace it    private(set) var messages: [Message] = [] // anyone can read; only TaskAgent can change    private(set) var isWorking = false    private var session: LanguageModelSession // nobody outside TaskAgent can even see it}
KeywordWho can read itWho can change itIn the app
(nothing), which means internalAny file in the appAny file in the app, if it's a varWorkspace.tasks, layout
private(set) varAny file in the appOnly code inside the typemessages, isWorking, actions
privateOnly code inside the type, in that fileOnly code inside the typesession, firstActionOfTurn, words(in:)
fileprivateAny code in the same fileSameNot used in Lite
publicOther modules tooOther modules too, if varUsed widely in Full (Full only)

Why private(set) matters here. The chat view shows agent.messages and the spinner reads agent.isWorking, so they can't be private. But if a view could write agent.isWorking = false, the screen could lie about what the agent is doing. private(set) allows reading everywhere and writing only inside TaskAgent.

private on view properties. You'll see @State private var draft = "" and @Environment(Workspace.self) private var workspace in every view. Apple recommends making view state private, because it belongs to that view alone and must not be set from outside.

let vs private(set) var. let can never change, even inside the type. private(set) var changes, but only from inside. workspace is a let because an agent always works on the same workspace; messages grows during a conversation.

Observation and SwiftUI state

SwiftUI redraws a view when data it reads changes. These attributes tell SwiftUI which data to watch, who owns it, and how views share it.

@Observable: a class SwiftUI can watch

@Observablefinal class Workspace {    var tasks: [TaskItem] = TaskItem.samples    var layout: BoardLayout = .grid}

@Observable is a macro: at compile time it adds tracking code to every property. When BoardView reads workspace.layout and the agent's tool later changes it, SwiftUI redraws only the views that read layout. That's why the board changes live while the agent works, with no extra code.

It goes on the line before class because it's an attribute of the whole class, like @MainActor. The order of the two doesn't matter. It only works on classes, not structs.

In the Full version, @ObservationIgnored marks a property SwiftUI shouldn't watch, such as the engine or a running Task (Full only).

@State: a value the view owns

@State private var sheet: Sheet?          // ContentView: which sheet is open@State private var draft = ""             // AgentPanel: what you're typing

A view struct is recreated on every redraw, so a plain var would be reset. @State keeps the value alive for as long as the view is on screen. Use it for small, local UI state.

The app also keeps its two main objects in @State, in WorkspaceAssistantApp, so they're created once and live as long as the app:

@State private var workspace: Workspace@State private var agent: TaskAgent init() {    let workspace = Workspace()    _workspace = State(initialValue: workspace)    _agent = State(initialValue: TaskAgent(workspace: workspace))}

The underscore form, _workspace, is the State wrapper itself. It's needed here because the agent must be built with the same workspace, so both are created together in init.

.environment(...) and @Environment: share an object with every view below

ContentView()    .environment(workspace)          // in the App: hand it down @Environment(Workspace.self) private var workspace   // in any view below: pick it up

Instead of passing workspace through every initializer, the app puts it in the environment once, and any view underneath can read it by type. @Environment(\.dismiss) in NewTaskSheet uses the same mechanism for a value SwiftUI provides: the action that closes the sheet.

@Bindable and $: two-way connections

var body: some View {    @Bindable var workspace = workspace    …    Picker("Layout", selection: $workspace.layout) { … }}

A control like Picker, Toggle or TextField needs a binding: something it can both read and write. The $ prefix makes one. $draft works directly on @State, but an object from @Environment can't make bindings by itself, so @Bindable var workspace = workspace wraps it first. Choosing a layout in the picker then writes straight into workspace.layout.

Other wrappers you'll meet

WrapperWhat it doesWhere
@FocusStateTrue while a text field has the keyboard; set it to false to hide the keyboardAgentPanel composer
@NamespaceAn ID space for matchedGeometryEffect, so tiles glide between layoutsBoardView
@BindingA read-write link to a value another view ownsBoardView's navigation path (Full only)
@ScaledMetricA size that grows with the user's text size settingTiles and pills (Full only)
@PreviewableLets a #Preview use @StatePreviews (Full only)

Concurrency: async, await, Task and @MainActor

The model takes seconds to answer, so asking it must not freeze the screen. Swift concurrency lets that work wait without blocking, and @MainActor keeps every change to the board on the main thread, where SwiftUI expects it.

async and await: functions that can pause

func send(_ text: String) async {    …    let response = try await session.respond(to: prompt)    messages.append(Message(role: .agent, text: response.content))}

async on a function means it can pause while it waits for something slow. await marks each place where it may pause. While send waits for the model, the app keeps scrolling, animating and redrawing; when the answer arrives, send carries on from the next line.

throws means a function can fail with an error, and try marks the call that might fail. try await is both: it may pause, and it may throw. The do { … } catch { … } around it in send turns a thrown error into a chat message.

Task { }: start async work from a button

Button("Send") {                      // simplified from AgentPanel    Task { await agent.send(text) }}

A button's action is ordinary, non-async code, so it can't await directly. Task { … } starts a new piece of async work and returns at once. The modifier .task { agent.prewarm() } on AgentPanel is the view version: it runs when the view appears and is cancelled when it disappears.

@MainActor: run on the main thread

@MainActor@Observablefinal class Workspace { … }

All UI updates must happen on the main thread. @MainActor on the class makes every property and method of Workspace and TaskAgent run there, and the compiler checks it: code that isn't on the main actor must await to reach them.

That's why each tool has an await that looks unnecessary:

struct AddTaskTool: Tool {    func call(arguments: Arguments) async throws -> String {        await workspace.addTask(title: arguments.title, …, by: .agent)    }}

Foundation Models calls tools away from the main thread. addTask belongs to the main actor, so the call must hop over to it, and await marks that hop. Without @MainActor, a tool and a tap could change tasks at the same moment and corrupt it; with it, they take turns.

defer: run this when the function exits

isWorking = truedefer { isWorking = false }

The defer block runs when send returns, by any path: a normal reply, the simulated agent's early return, or an error. The spinner can never get stuck on.

In the Full version (Full only)

You seeMeaning
SendableThe type is safe to pass between threads; most value types qualify automatically
nonisolatedNot tied to the main actor, so it can be used from any thread, e.g. constants like Spacing
Task<Void, Never>?A stored handle to running work, so it can be cancelled with .cancel()
Task { [weak self] in … }The task doesn't keep the view model alive if the screen goes away

Foundation Models: @Generable, @Guide, Tool and the session

These come from Apple's FoundationModels framework, which runs the on-device model. @Generable is the most important: it lets the model produce a Swift value instead of free text.

@Generable: a type the model can fill in

@Generableenum TaskCategory: String, CaseIterable {    case development, testing, design, operations}

@Generable is a macro that describes the type to the model and constrains its output while it generates. The model normally writes any text it likes; for a @Generable type it can only produce valid values. For TaskCategory that means exactly one of the four cases, never "Dev" or "Testing work". This is called guided generation.

It's used in two ways in the app:

  1. On the enums TaskCategory and BoardLayout, so the model can pick them as tool arguments.
  2. On each tool's Arguments struct, so every tool call arrives as a typed Swift value.

In TaskSynthesiser the same macro goes on a whole result struct, and respond(to:generating: ProjectBlueprint.self) returns a filled-in ProjectBlueprint.

@Guide: describe or limit one property

@Generablestruct Arguments {    @Guide(description: "A short task title in Title Case, e.g. 'Review Pull Requests'")    var title: String    var category: TaskCategory    @Guide(description: "True only if the user says the task is important, urgent or high priority")    var highPriority: Bool}

@Guide tells the model what a property means, in plain English. It can also add hard limits: @Guide(.range(1...30)) for numbers, or @Guide(.count(3)) for arrays. A property without @Guide, like category, is described by its name and type alone.

Tool: a function the model may call

struct AddTaskTool: Tool {    let name = "addTask"    let description = "Adds a new task to the board."    let workspace: Workspace     @Generable struct Arguments { … }     func call(arguments: Arguments) async throws -> String {        await workspace.addTask(title: arguments.title, category: arguments.category,                                highPriority: arguments.highPriority, by: .agent)    }}

Tool is a protocol with four requirements:

PartRead byPurpose
nameThe modelHow it refers to the tool
descriptionThe modelWhen it should use it
ArgumentsThe model fills it inWhat it must provide; @Generable, so always valid
call(arguments:)Your Swift codeDoes the real work and returns what happened

The returned String goes back to the model, which reads it before answering. That's why Workspace commands return honest sentences like "“X” was already done. Nothing changed."

LanguageModelSession: one conversation

let tools: [any Tool] = [AddTaskTool(workspace: workspace), …]let session = LanguageModelSession(model: SystemLanguageModel.default, tools: tools, instructions: instructions) let response = try await session.respond(to: prompt)let reply = response.content

A session holds the instructions, the tools and the whole conversation so far, so follow-ups like "and the other one" make sense. respond(to:) is where the agent loop happens: the model may call several tools, read each result, and only then write response.content.

[any Tool] means "an array of values of any type that conforms to Tool"; the four tools are different structs, so any is needed to put them in one array.

Also in TaskAgentMeaning
SystemLanguageModel.default.availabilityWhether the model can run, and if not, why
session.prewarm()Loads the model early so the first reply is faster
LanguageModelSession.GenerationErrorErrors such as .exceededContextWindowSize (conversation too long) or .guardrailViolation

SwiftData: saving tasks (Full only)

Lite keeps tasks in memory, and they reset when the app restarts. Full saves them with SwiftData, behind its own TaskRepository protocol, so the rest of the app never touches the database directly.

@Model: a class SwiftData stores

@Modelfinal class TaskRecord {    var id: UUID = UUID()    var title: String = ""    var categoryRaw: String = TaskCategory.development.rawValue    var stepsData: Data = Data()    …}

@Model is a macro, like @Observable, that turns a class into a stored table: each property becomes a column. It must be a class, which is why TaskRecord is a final class while the app's own TaskItem stays a struct. Enums are stored as their raw strings (categoryRaw) and the steps as encoded Data, so the stored format doesn't depend on app types. Every property has a default, which is what CloudKit sync would need later.

ModelContainer, ModelContext and #Predicate

container = try ModelContainer(for: TaskRecord.self, configurations: configuration) try context.fetch(FetchDescriptor<TaskRecord>(sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\.sortIndex)]))try context.delete(model: TaskRecord.self, where: #Predicate { ids.contains($0.id) })try context.save()
PieceRole
ModelContainerThe database itself, set up for TaskRecord; isStoredInMemoryOnly: true for tests
ModelContextThe workspace you read and change records through: fetch, insert, delete, save
FetchDescriptorWhat to fetch, filtered and sorted
#Predicate { … }A filter the database can run, written as Swift; here, records whose id is in ids

You'll often see @Query in SwiftData tutorials: a view property that fetches and stays up to date. Full doesn't use it, because views get tasks from the view models, not from the database. TaskSynthesiser stores its blueprints with SwiftData too.

SwiftUI view syntax

A SwiftUI view is a struct with a body that describes the screen. SwiftUI calls body again whenever data it reads changes, and works out what to redraw.

@main, App and Scene: where the app starts

@mainstruct WorkspaceAssistantApp: App {    var body: some Scene {        WindowGroup { ContentView() }    }}

@main marks the app's entry point; there's exactly one. An App's body returns a Scene, and WindowGroup is the scene that shows your first view.

some View: "a specific view, I won't spell it out"

var body: some View { … }private func column(_ title: String, _ tasks: [TaskItem]) -> some View { … }

Every view's real type is long and nested, such as a ScrollView of a Group of a LazyVGrid. some View means "one specific type that conforms to View; the compiler knows which". You get the speed of a concrete type without writing it. Compare any Tool, which allows a different type for each element.

@ViewBuilder: return different views from if or switch

@ViewBuilder private var badge: some View {    if task.isHighPriority && !task.isDone {        Image(systemName: "star.fill").foregroundStyle(.yellow)    }}

body already allows if, switch and several views in a row. A property or function you write yourself needs @ViewBuilder to work the same way. Here badge is a star, or nothing; in TaskTile, content is a different layout for each style.

Modifiers: each line wraps the view in another

Text(title)    .font(.caption.bold())    .textCase(.uppercase)    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)

Each .modifier() returns a new view wrapping the previous one, so order matters: .padding() then .background() colours the padding too, while the reverse doesn't. A few modifiers in the app that are worth knowing:

ModifierWhat it does
.animation(.spring(…), value: workspace.tasks)Animates every change caused by tasks changing, including the agent's
.matchedGeometryEffect(id: task.id, in: tiles)Moves the same tile smoothly between grid, list and board
.sheet(item: $sheet)Shows a sheet while sheet isn't nil; setting it back to nil closes it
.safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom)Pins the "Ask the Agent" button above the bottom edge, and scrolls content clear of it
.sensoryFeedback(.success, trigger: …)A haptic tap each time the agent does something
.task { … }Runs async work when the view appears

ForEach: one view per item

ForEach(workspace.orderedTasks) { tile($0, style: .tile) }ForEach(BoardLayout.allCases, id: \.self) { layout in … }

ForEach needs to tell items apart. TaskItem is Identifiable, so its id is used. Enum cases have no id, so id: \.self says "each value is its own ID".

#Preview: a canvas preview

#Preview {    let workspace = Workspace()    ContentView()        .environment(workspace)        .environment(TaskAgent(workspace: workspace))}

#Preview is a macro that shows the view in Xcode's canvas. It isn't part of the running app. A preview must provide everything the view reads from the environment, or it crashes.

Everyday Swift syntax

The shorthand below appears on almost every page of the tutorials. Most of it is in Workspace.swift.

Optionals: a value that might be missing

func index(of id: TaskItem.ID) -> Int? {          // Int? = an Int, or nil    tasks.firstIndex { $0.id == id }} guard let index = index(of: id) else { return "That task no longer exists." }tasks[index].isDone = true                         // from here on, index is a plain Int
You seeMeaning
Int?, Sheet?Optional: holds a value or nil
guard let x = … else { return }Unwrap, or leave early; x is usable for the rest of the function. The app uses it to reject bad input first
if let x = … { }Unwrap; x exists only inside the braces
a ?? ba if it isn't nil, otherwise b
if case .exceededContextWindowSize = errorChecks whether a value matches one enum case
catch let error as GenerationErrorCatches only that error type, already cast

Closures: short inline functions

tasks.filter { !$0.isDone }          // $0 = the first argument: each tasktasks.filter(\.isDone)               // key path: "the isDone of each task"tasks.map(\.title).joined(separator: ", ")

A closure is a function without a name, written in braces. When it's the last argument, it goes after the parentheses (a trailing closure), which is why you see Button("Delete") { … } and filter { … }. $0, $1 are the closure's arguments when you don't name them; { layout in … } names it. \.isDone is a key path, a shorter way to say "read this property from each item".

Functions and properties

You seeMeaningExample
Argument labelsNames used at the call siteswitchLayout(to: .list, by: .agent)
_ before a parameterNo label at the call sitecomplete(_ id:) is called as complete(id, by: .user)
@discardableResultNo warning if the caller ignores the return valueTaps ignore the sentence; tools return it to the model
Computed propertyCalculated each time it's read, not storedvar orderedTasks: [TaskItem] { … }
init(…)Sets up a new instanceTaskAgent.init(workspace:)
self.workspace = workspaceself. separates the property from the parameter with the same nameTaskAgent.init
Self.words(in:)Calls a static member of the current typeWorkspace.findTask
.toggle()Flips a Booltasks[index].isDone.toggle()

Strings and expressions

You seeMeaning
"Added \(title)"String interpolation: inserts a value into the text

Tutorial 1 of 6 · 20 min

Modelling the Board

Every agent needs something to act on. Start with the data: tasks, their categories, and a Workspace class that is the only place the board can change.

Meet a keyword you don't know? Look it up in the Swift Code Guide.

Download Project Files

Section 1

Describe a Task

Create a new iOS App project named WorkspaceAssistant in Xcode 26 or later, with SwiftUI and iOS 26 as the deployment target. Add a Model folder.

A task has a title, a category and two flags. The category and the layout are enums marked @Generable, so the model can use them directly as tool arguments later.

  1. Step 1

    Create TaskItem.swift with the TaskItem struct and the TaskCategory enum. Because TaskCategory is @Generable, the model will only ever be able to choose one of these four values.

    TaskItem.swift
    1import Foundation2import FoundationModels3 4/// One task on the board.5struct TaskItem: Identifiable, Hashable {6    let id = UUID()7    var title: String8    var category: TaskCategory9    var isHighPriority = false10    var isDone = false11    /// Goes up by one on every change, so the tile knows when to pulse.12    var revision = 013}14 15/// The kind of work a task is.16///17/// `@Generable` lets this enum be used directly as a tool argument:18/// the model can only ever pick one of these four values.19@Generable20enum TaskCategory: String, CaseIterable {21    case development, testing, design, operations22}

  2. Step 2

    Add BoardLayout, also @Generable, so the agent will be able to change how the board looks.

    TaskItem.swift
    ⋯1import Foundation2import FoundationModels3 4/// One task on the board.5struct TaskItem: Identifiable, Hashable {6    let id = UUID()7    var title: String8    var category: TaskCategory9    var isHighPriority = false10    var isDone = false11    /// Goes up by one on every change, so the tile knows when to pulse.12    var revision = 013}14 15/// The kind of work a task is.16///17/// `@Generable` lets this enum be used directly as a tool argument:18/// the model can only ever pick one of these four values.19@Generable20enum TaskCategory: String, CaseIterable {21    case development, testing, design, operations22}23 24/// How the board is drawn. Also `@Generable`, so the agent can change it.25@Generable26enum BoardLayout: String, CaseIterable {27    case grid, list, board28}

  3. Step 3

    Add the sample tasks every demo starts from. revision goes up on every change; the tiles will use it to pulse.

    TaskItem.swift

Also `@Generable`, so the agent can change it.25@Generable26enum BoardLayout: String, CaseIterable {27    case grid, list, board28}29 30extension TaskItem {31    /// The board every demo starts from.32    static let samples: [TaskItem] = [33        TaskItem(title: "Refactor Network Layer", category: .development),34        TaskItem(title: "Write Unit Test Suite", category: .testing),35        TaskItem(title: "Redesign Onboarding Flow", category: .design),36        TaskItem(title: "Set Up CI/CD Pipeline", category: .operations),37        TaskItem(title: "Fix Memory Leak in Feed", category: .development),38        TaskItem(title: "Accessibility Audit", category: .testing),39    ]40}

Section 2

Create the Workspace

Workspace holds the board and is the only place it changes. Each change is a command method. Later, the user's taps and the agent's tools will call exactly these methods, so the AI can never do anything the user couldn't.

  1. Step 1

    Create Workspace.swift. AgentAction records what the agent did, ChangedBy tells a tap from a tool call, and orderedTasks puts high-priority tasks first.

    Workspace.swift
    1import Foundation2import Observation3 4/// Something the agent did, shown as a chip in the chat.5struct AgentAction: Identifiable, Hashable {6    let id = UUID()7    let symbol: String8    let summary: String9}10 11/// Who made a change: a tap in the UI, or a tool call by the agent.12enum ChangedBy {13    case user, agent14}15 16/// The app's state, and the only place it changes.17///18/// Every change is a "command" method.   2. Step 2

    Add the first command, addTask, and the record helper. Every command returns a short sentence. When the agent calls a tool, that sentence is all the model sees of what happened, so it must be true.

Section 3

Let the Agent Name Tasks in Its Own Words

The model doesn't know task IDs. It will say "the unit tests". Give the agent its own way in: turn the words into one task, then run the same command a tap would.

  1. Step 1

    Add findTask, which matches words like "unit tests" to "Write Unit Test Suite". It returns nil when nothing matches, or when more than one task does. problem then tells the model honestly what went wrong, so it can ask the user instead of guessing.

Tutorial 2 of 6 · 25 min

Drawing the Board

Draw the board in SwiftUI. Because the views only read Workspace, every change, whether from a tap or from the agent, animates in by itself.

Download Project Files

Section 1

Draw a Task Tile

Add a Views folder. A tile is drawn in one of three styles: a large tile for the grid, a row for the list, and a compact card for the board's columns.

  1. Step 1

    Create BoardView.swift and add TaskTile, plus a colour and a symbol for every category and layout.

    BoardView.swift
    1import SwiftUI2 3/// One coloured task tile.4struct TaskTile: View {5    enum Style { case tile, row, compact }6 7    let task: TaskItem8    let style: Style9 10    var body: some View {11        content12            .foregroundStyle(.white)13            .padding(style == .compact ? 10 : 14)14            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: style == .tile ? 120 : nil, alignment: .topLeading)15            .background(task.category.color.gradient, in: .rect(cornerRadius: style == .compact ? 14 : 22))16            .saturation(task.isDone ? 0.1 : 1)17            .opacity(task.isDone ? 0.7 : 1)18    }19 20    @ViewBuilder private var content: some View {21        switch style {22        case .tile:23            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 6) {24                HStack { glyph; Spacer(); badge }25                Spacer(minLength: 0)26                Text(task.title).font(.headline)27                Text(task.category.rawValue.capitalized).font(.caption.weight(.medium)).opacity(0.8)28            }29        case .row:30            HStack(spacing: 12) {31                glyph32                VStack(alignment: .leading) {33                    Text(task.title).font(.headline)34                    Text(task.category.rawValue.capitalized).font(.caption.weight(.medium)).opacity(0.8)35                }36                Spacer()37                badge38            }39        case .compact:40            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 6) {41                HStack { Image(systemName: symbol).font(.subheadline.bold()); Spacer(); badge }42                Text(task.title).font(.caption.weight(.semibold)).lineLimit(3)43            }44        }45    }46 47    private var symbol: String { task.isDone ? "checkmark" : task.category.symbol }48 49    private var glyph: some View {50        Image(systemName: symbol)51            .font(.title3.weight(.semibold))52            .frame(width: 40, height: 40)53            .background(.black.opacity(0.15), in: .circle)54    }55 56    @ViewBuilder private var badge: some View {57        if task.isHighPriority && !task.isDone {58            Image(systemName: "star.fill").foregroundStyle(.yellow)59        }60    }61}62 63extension TaskCategory {64    var color: Color {65        switch self {66        case .development: .blue67        case .testing: .green68        case .design: .pink69        case .operations: .orange70        }71    }72 73    var symbol: String {74        switch self {75        case .development: "hammer.fill"76        case .testing: "checkmark.seal.fill"77        case .design: "paintbrush.pointed.fill"78        case .operations: "gearshape.2.fill"79        }80    }81}82 83extension BoardLayout {84    var symbol: String {85        switch self {86        case .grid: "square.grid.2x2"87        case .list: "list.bullet"88        case .board: "rectangle.split.3x1"89        }90    }91}

  2. Step 2

    Make the tile pulse whenever its task changes. revision goes up on every change, so phaseAnimator fires once per change, whoever made it, and the icon bounces with symbolEffect.

    BoardView.swift
    1import SwiftUI2 3/// One coloured task tile. Show the Board

Put the board on screen, with a menu to switch layout or start again, and create the workspace once for the whole app.

Tutorial 3 of 6 · 15 min

Giving the Agent Tools

A tool is a Swift function the model may decide to call. Write four of them, each a thin adapter over one Workspace command.

Download Project Files

Section 1

Write the Four Tools

Every tool has three parts. Its name and description tell the model when to use it. Its @Generable Arguments say what the model must fill in. Its call(arguments:) runs your code and returns what really happened.

Add an Agent folder for the agent's files.

  1. Step 1

    Create Tools.swift and add AddTaskTool. @Guide describes each argument to the model, and category reuses the @Generable enum from the model layer.

    Tools.swift
    1import FoundationModels2 3// The agent's four tools.4//5// A tool is a function the model may decide to call. You give it:6//   • a name and a description  → how the model knows WHEN to use it7//   • @Generable Arguments      → what the model must fill in (it can't invent other fields)8//   • call(arguments:)          → your Swift code, which returns what really happened9//10// Each tool here is a thin adapter over one Workspace command.11 12struct AddTaskTool: Tool {13    let name = "addTask"14    let description = "Adds a new task to the board."15    let workspace: Workspace16 17    @Generable18    struct Arguments {19        @Guide(description: "A short task title in Title Case, e.g. 'Review Pull Requests'")20        var title: String21        var category: TaskCategory22        @Guide(description: "True only if the user says the task is important, urgent or high priority")23        var highPriority: Bool24    }25 26    func call(arguments: Arguments) async throws -> String {27        await workspace.addTask(title: arguments.title, category: arguments.category, highPriority: arguments.highPriority, by: .agent)28    }29}

  2. Step 2

    Add CompleteTaskTool. The model passes the user's own words, such as "unit tests", and completeTask turns them into one task. The await is needed because Workspace lives on the main actor.

    Tools.swift
    ⋯1import FoundationModels2 3// The agent's four tools.4//5// A tool is a function the model may decide to call. You give it:6//   • a name and a description  → how the model knows WHEN to use it7//   • @Generable Arguments      → what the model must fill in (it can't invent other fields)8//   • call(arguments:)          → your Swift code, which returns what really happened9//10// Each tool here is a thin adapter over one Workspace command.11 12struct AddTaskTool: Tool {13    let name = "addTask"14    let description = "Adds a new task to the board."15    let workspace: Workspace16 17    @Generable18    struct Arguments {19        @Guide(description: "A short task title in Title Case, e.g. 'Review Pull Requests'")20        var title: String21        var category: TaskCategory22        @Guide(description: "True only if the user says the task is important, urgent or high priority")23        var highPriority: Bool24    }25 26    func call(arguments: Arguments) async throws -> String {27        await workspace.addTask(title: arguments.title, category: arguments.category, highPriority: arguments.highPriority, by: .agent)28    }29}30 31struct CompleteTaskTool: Tool {32    let name = "completeTask"33    let description = "Marks an existing task as done."34    let workspace: Workspace35 36    @Generable37    struct Arguments {38        @Guide(description: "The user's words for the task, e.g. 'unit tests'")39        var task: String40    }41 42    func call(arguments: Arguments) async throws -> String {43        await workspace.completeTask(arguments.task)44    }45}

Tutorial 4 of 6 · 25 min

Talking to the Agent

Create a LanguageModelSession with the tools, send it the user's request, and show each tool call in a chat while the board changes behind it.

Download Project Files

Section 1

Create the Session

TaskAgent owns one on-device LanguageModelSession. The session holds the tools, the instructions and the conversation so far.

  1. Step 1

    Create TaskAgent.swift. makeSession registers the four tools and writes the instructions, including the tasks on the board, so the model knows their names.

    TaskAgent.swift
    1import Foundation2import FoundationModels3import Observation4 5/// The agent: one on-device `LanguageModelSession` that holds the conversation and the tools.6///7/// The agentic loop lives inside `session.respond(to:)`. For one prompt the model may call several8/// tools, read what each one returned, and only then write its reply. We just watch it happen.9@MainActor10@Observable11final class TaskAgent {12    struct Message: Identifiable {13        enum Role { case user, agent, problem }14        let id = UUID()15        let role: Role16        let text: String17        var actions: [AgentAction] = []18    }19 20    let workspace: Workspace21    private(set) var messages: [Message] = []22    private(set) var isWorking = false23    private var firstActionOfTurn = 024    private var session: LanguageModelSession25 26    init(workspace: Workspace) {27        self.workspace = workspace28        session = Self.makeSession(for: workspace)29    }30 31    // MARK: - Session32 33    private static func makeSession(for workspace: Workspace) -> LanguageModelSession {34        let tools: [any Tool] = [35            AddTaskTool(workspace: workspace),36            CompleteTaskTool(workspace: workspace),37            PrioritizeTaskTool(workspace: workspace),38            SwitchLayoutTool(workspace: workspace),39        ]40        let titles = workspace.tasks.map(\.title).joined(separator: ", ")41        let instructions = """42        You are an agent inside a task-board app. You change the board ONLY by calling tools.43        - Call a tool for every change the user asks for. One request may need several tools.44        - To refer to a task, pass the user's own words for it.45        - Read every tool result. Only say something happened if a tool result says it did.46        - Reply in one short, friendly sentence.47        Tasks on the board when this conversation started: \(titles).48        """49        return LanguageModelSession(model: SystemLanguageModel.default, tools: tools, instructions: instructions)50    }51}

  2. Step 2

    Add newConversation and prewarm, plus unavailableReason. It checks SystemLanguageModel.default.availability and explains why Apple Intelligence can't run, for example when it's switched off.

    TaskAgent.swift
    ⋯1import Foundation2import FoundationModels3import Observation4 5/// The agent: one on-device `LanguageModelSession` that holds the conversation and the tools.6///7/// The agentic loop lives inside `session.respond(to:)`. For one prompt the model may call several8/// tools, read what each one returned, and only then write its reply. We just watch it happen.9@MainActor10@Observable11final class TaskAgent {12    struct Message: Identifiable {13        enum Role { case user, agent, problem }14        let id = UUID()15        let role: Role16        let text: String17        var actions: [AgentAction] = []18    }19 20    let workspace: Workspace21    private(set) var messages: [Message] = []22    private(set) var isWorking = false23    private var firstActionOfTurn = 024    private var session: LanguageModelSession25 26    init(workspace: Workspace) {27        self.workspace = workspace28        session = Self.makeSession(for: workspace)29    }30 31    // MARK: - Session32 33    private static func makeSession(for workspace: Workspace) -> LanguageModelSession {34        let tools: [any Tool] = [35            AddTaskTool(workspace: workspace),36            CompleteTaskTool(workspace: workspace),37            PrioritizeTaskTool(workspace: workspace),38            SwitchLayoutTool(workspace: workspace),39        ]40        let titles = workspace.tasks.map(\.title).joined(separator: ", ")41        let instructions = """42        You are an agent inside a task-board app. You change the board ONLY by calling tools.43        - Call a tool for every change the user asks for. One request may need several tools.44        - To refer to a task, pass the user's own words for it.45        - Read every tool result. Only say something happened if a tool result says it did.46        - Reply in one short, friendly sentence.47        Tasks on the board when this conversation started: \(titles).48        """49        return LanguageModelSession(model: SystemLanguageModel.default, tools: tools, instructions: instructions)50    }51 52    /// Forgets the conversation. The board is not touched.53    func newConversation() {54        messages.removeAll()55        session = Self.makeSession(for: workspace)56    }57 58    /// Loads the model early so the first reply is faster.59    func prewarm() {60        if unavailableReason == nil { session.prewarm() }61    }62 63    // MARK: - Availability64 65    /// `nil` when Apple Intelligence is ready, otherwise what to tell the user.66    var unavailableReason: String? {67        switch SystemLanguageModel.default.availability {68        case .available:69            nil70        case .unavailable(.deviceNotEligible):71            "This device doesn’t support Apple Intelligence."72        case .unavailable(.appleIntelligenceNotEnabled):73            "Turn on Apple Intelligence in Settings to use the agent."74        case .unavailable(.modelNotReady):75            "Apple Intelligence is still downloading. Try again in a few minutes."76        case .unavailable:77            "Apple Intelligence isn’t available right now."78        }79    }80}

Section 2

Run the Agentic Loop

The agentic loop lives inside a single call. For one prompt, the model may call several tools, read what each returned, and only then write its reply. You just watch it happen.

  1. Step 1

    Add send(_:), which calls respond(to:). liveActions are the actions logged since this turn began; they appear as chips while the model is still working.

    TaskAgent.swift
    ⋯1import Foundation2import FoundationModels3import Observation4 5/// The agent: one on-device `LanguageModelSession` that holds the conversation and the tools.6///7/// The agentic loop lives inside `session.respond(to:)`. For one prompt the model may call several8/// tools, read what each one returned, and only then write its reply. We just watch it happen.9@MainActor10@Observable11final class TaskAgent {12    struct Message: Identifiable {13        enum Role { case user, agent, problem }14        let id = UUID()15        let role: Role16        let text: String17        var actions: [AgentAction] = []18    }19 20    let workspace: Workspace21    private(set) var messages: [Message] = []22    private(set) var isWorking = false23    private var firstActionOfTurn = 024    private var session: LanguageModelSession25 26    init(workspace: Workspace) {27        self.workspace = workspace28        session = Self.makeSession(for: workspace)29    }30 31    // MARK: - Session32 33    private static func makeSession(for workspace: Workspace) -> LanguageModelSession {34        let tools: [any Tool] = [35            AddTaskTool(workspace: workspace),36            CompleteTaskTool(workspace: workspace),37            PrioritizeTaskTool(workspace: workspace),38            SwitchLayoutTool(workspace: workspace),39        ]40        let titles = workspace.tasks.map(\.title).joined(separator: ", ")41        let instructions = """42        You are an agent inside a task-board app. You change the board ONLY by calling tools.43        - Call a tool for every change the user asks for. One request may need several tools.44        - To refer to a task, pass the user's own words for it.45        - Read every tool result. Only say something happened if a tool result says it did.46        - Reply in one short, friendly sentence.47        Tasks on the board when this conversation started: \(titles).48        """49        return LanguageModelSession(model: SystemLanguageModel.default, tools: tools, instructions: instructions)50    }51 52    /// Forgets the conversation. The board is not touched.53    func newConversation() {54        messages.removeAll()55        session = Self.makeSession(for: workspace)56    }57 58    /// Loads the model early so the first reply is faster.59    func prewarm() {60        if unavailableReason == nil { session.prewarm() }61    }62 63    // MARK: - Talking to the model64 65    /// What the tools have done so far in the current turn, shown live while the model works.66    var liveActions: [AgentAction] {67        isWorking ? Array(workspace.actions.dropFirst(firstActionOfTurn)) : []68    }69 70    func send(_ text: String) async {71        let prompt = text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)72        guard !prompt.isEmpty, !isWorking else { return }73        messages.append(Message(role: .user, text: prompt))74        firstActionOfTurn = workspace.actions.count75        isWorking = true76        defer { isWorking = false }77 78        do {79            let response = try await session.respond(to: prompt)80            messages.append(Message(role: .agent, text: response.content, actions: liveActions))81        } catch {82            messages.append(Message(role: .problem, text: error.localizedDescription, actions: liveActions))83        }84    }85 86    // MARK: - Availability87 88    /// `nil` when Apple Intelligence is ready, otherwise what to tell the user.⋯89    var unavailableReason: String? {90        switch SystemLanguageModel.default.availability {91        case .available:92            nil93        case .unavailable(.deviceNotEligible):94            "This device doesn’t support Apple Intelligence."95        case .unavailable(.appleIntelligenceNotEnabled):96            "Turn on Apple Intelligence in Settings to use the agent."97        case .unavailable(.modelNotReady):98            "Apple Intelligence is still downloading. Try again in a few minutes."99        case .unavailable:100            "Apple Intelligence isn’t available right now."101        }102    }103}

One request may need several tools.44        - To refer to a task, pass the user's own words for it.45        - Read every tool result. Only say something happened if a tool result says it did.46        - Reply in one short, friendly sentence.47        Tasks on the board when this conversation started: \(titles).48        """49        return LanguageModelSession(model: SystemLanguageModel.default, tools: tools, instructions: instructions)50    }51 52    /// Forgets the conversation. The board is not touched.53    func newConversation() {54        messages.removeAll()55        session = Self.makeSession(for: workspace)56    }57 58    /// Loads the model early so the first reply is faster.59    func prewarm() {60        if unavailableReason == nil { session.prewarm() }61    }62 63    // MARK: - Talking to the model64 65    /// What the tools have done so far in the current turn, shown live while the model works.66    var liveActions: [AgentAction] {67        isWorking ? Array(workspace.actions.dropFirst(firstActionOfTurn)) : []68    }69 70    func send(_ text: String) async {71        let prompt = text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)72        guard !prompt.isEmpty, !isWorking else { return }73        messages.append(Message(role: .user, text: prompt))74        firstActionOfTurn = workspace.actions.count75        isWorking = true76        defer { isWorking = false }77 78        do {79            let response = try await session.respond(to: prompt)80            messages.append(Message(role: .agent, text: response.content, actions: liveActions))81        } catch let error as LanguageModelSession.GenerationError {82            var text = error.localizedDescription83            if case .exceededContextWindowSize = error {84                // The on-device model has a small context window. Please try again."87            }88            messages.append(Message(role: .problem, text: text, actions: liveActions))89        } catch {90            messages.append(Message(role: .problem, text: error.localizedDescription, actions: liveActions))91        }⋯92    }93 94    // MARK: - Availability95 96    /// `nil` when Apple Intelligence is ready, otherwise what to tell the user.97    var unavailableReason: String? {98        switch SystemLanguageModel.default.availability {99        case .available:100            nil101        case .unavailable(.deviceNotEligible):102            "This device doesn’t support Apple Intelligence."103        case .unavailable(.appleIntelligenceNotEnabled):104            "Turn on Apple Intelligence in Settings to use the agent."105        case .unavailable(.modelNotReady):106            "Apple Intelligence is still downloading. Try again in a few minutes."107        case .unavailable:108            "Apple Intelligence isn’t available right now."109        }110    }111}

"checkmark" : task.category.symbol }117 118    private var glyph: some View {119        Image(systemName: symbol)120            .font(.title3.weight(.semibold))121            .frame(width: 40, height: 40)122            .background(.black.opacity(0.15), in: .circle)123            .symbolEffect(.bounce, value: task.revision)124    }125 126    @ViewBuilder private var badge: some View {127        if task.isHighPriority && !task.isDone {128            Image(systemName: "star.fill").foregroundStyle(.yellow)129        }130    }131}132 133extension TaskCategory {134    var color: Color {135        switch self {136        case .development: .blue137        case .testing: .green138        case .design: .pink139        case .operations: .orange140        }141    }142 143    var symbol: String {144        switch self {145        case .development: "hammer.fill"146        case .testing: "checkmark.seal.fill"147        case .design: "paintbrush.pointed.fill"148        case .operations: "gearshape.2.fill"149        }150    }151}152 153extension BoardLayout {154    var symbol: String {155        switch self {156        case .grid: "square.grid.2x2"157        case .list: "list.bullet"158        case .board: "rectangle.split.3x1"159        }160    }161}

Section 3

Keep the Demo Working on Any Mac

The simulator uses the Mac's Apple Intelligence, so on a Mac where it's turned off or unsupported the agent can't run. A simple stand-in keeps the demo working, clearly labelled so nobody mistakes it for the model.

  1. Step 1

    Add SimulatedAgent.swift to the Agent folder. It isn't AI: it spots keywords such as "finished" or "board" and calls the same Workspace commands as the real tools, with short pauses so changes land one at a time.

    SimulatedAgent.swift
    1import Foundation2 3/// A stand-in for the on-device model, used only when Apple Intelligence isn't available4/// (for example a simulator on a Mac with Apple Intelligence turned off).5///6/// It is NOT AI. It spots a few keywords and calls the same Workspace commands the real tools call,7/// so the demo still works. It only knows the four built-in tools; tools you add need the real model.8/// You never need to open this file while teaching.9@MainActor10enum SimulatedAgent {11    private enum Intent { case add, complete, prioritize }12 13    static func respond(to prompt: String, workspace: Workspace) async -> String {14        var results: [String] = []15        var lastIntent: Intent?16 17        // "Prioritise the leak and show the board" → one clause per action.18        for clause in clauses(in: prompt) {19            let words = tokens(in: clause)20 21            if let layout = detectedLayout(in: words) {22                await think()23                results.append(workspace.switchLayout(to: layout, by: .agent))24                continue25            }26            // "I finished the tests and the pipeline": the second clause reuses the last verb.27            guard let intent = detectedIntent(in: words) ?? lastIntent else { continue }28            lastIntent = intent29            await think()30            switch intent {31            case .add:32                results.append(workspace.addTask(title: makeTitle(from: words), category: category(for: words), highPriority: isUrgent(words), by: .agent))33            case .complete:34                results.append(workspace.completeTask(taskWords(words)))35            case .prioritize:36                results.append(workspace.prioritizeTask(taskWords(words)))37            }38        }39 40        await think()41        guard !results.isEmpty else {42            return "I’m the simulated agent, so I only understand simple requests, for example “prioritise the memory leak” or “show the board”."43        }44        return results.map(firstSentence).joined(separator: " ")45    }46 47    // MARK: - Keyword spotting48 49    private static func detectedIntent(in words: [String]) -> Intent? {50        if words.contains(where: { ["add", "create", "new"].contains($0) }) { return .add }51        if words.contains(where: { $0.hasPrefix("priorit") || ["important", "urgent"].contains($0) }) { return .prioritize }52        if words.contains(where: { ["done", "finished", "finish", "complete", "completed"].contains($0) }) { return .complete }53        return nil54    }55 56    private static func detectedLayout(in words: [String]) -> BoardLayout? {57        let wantsLayout = words.contains { ["show", "switch", "view", "layout", "display", "change"].contains($0) }58        guard wantsLayout || words.count <= 2 else { return nil }59        if words.contains("board") || words.contains("columns") || words.contains("kanban") { return .board }60        if words.contains("list") { return .list }61        if words.contains("grid") || words.contains("tiles") { return .grid }62        return nil63    }64 65    /// "add a high-priority task to review pull requests" → "Review Pull Requests"66    /// "add a design review task" → "Design Review"67    private static func makeTitle(from words: [String]) -> String {68        var rest = words69        if let taskIndex = rest.firstIndex(where: { $0 == "task" || $0 == "tasks" }) {70            let after = Array(rest[(taskIndex + 1)...])71            if let first = after.first, ["to", "for", "called", "named", "about"].contains(first), after.count > 1 {72                rest = Array(after.dropFirst())73            } else {74                rest = Array(rest[..<taskIndex])75            }76        }77        let filler: Set<String> = ["add", "create", "new", "a", "an", "the", "high", "priority", "urgent", "important", "please", "me", "my"]78        let kept = rest.filter { !filler.contains($0) }79        return kept.isEmpty ? "New Task" : kept.map(\.capitalized).joined(separator: " ")80    }81 82    /// The words that name the task, e.g. "i finished the unit tests" → "unit tests".83    private static func taskWords(_ words: [String]) -> String {84        let filler: Set<String> = [85            "i", "ve", "m", "s", "we", "the", "a", "an", "my", "mark", "set", "make", "as", "is", "are", "it", "to",86            "now", "too", "also", "please", "have", "has", "been", "just", "done", "finished", "finish",87            "complete", "completed", "important", "urgent", "high", "priority", "task", "tasks",88        ]89        return words.filter { !filler.contains($0) && !$0.hasPrefix("priorit") }.joined(separator: " ")90    }91 92    private static func category(for words: [String]) -> TaskCategory {93        if words.contains(where: { $0.hasPrefix("test") || ["qa", "bug", "audit"].contains($0) }) { return .testing }94        if words.contains(where: { ["design", "ui", "ux", "icon", "mockup", "onboarding"].contains($0) }) { return .design }95        if words.contains(where: { ["deploy", "release", "server", "pipeline", "ci", "build", "backup"].contains($0) }) { return .operations }96        return .development97    }98 99    private static func isUrgent(_ words: [String]) -> Bool {100        words.contains("urgent") || words.contains("important") || words.contains("priority")101    }102 103    // MARK: - Text helpers104 105    private static func clauses(in prompt: String) -> [String] {106        var text = prompt.lowercased()107        for separator in [" and then ", " then ", " and ", ",", ";", "."] {108            text = text.replacingOccurrences(of: separator, with: "|")109        }110        return text.split(separator: "|").map(String.init)111    }112 113    private static func tokens(in text: String) -> [String] {114        text.lowercased().split { !$0.isLetter && !$0.isNumber }.map(String.init)115    }116 117    private static func firstSentence(_ text: String) -> String {118        let sentence = text.components(separatedBy: ". ").first ?? text119        return sentence.hasSuffix(".") ? sentence : sentence + "."120    }121 122    /// A short pause so each change lands one at a time, like the real agent.123    private static func think() async {124        try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(700))125    }126}

  2. Step 2

    In send(_:), use the simulated agent when unavailableReason isn't nil.

    TaskAgent.swift
    ⋯1import Foundation2import FoundationModels3import Observation4 5/// The agent: one on-device `LanguageModelSession` that holds the conversation and the tools.6///7/// The agentic loop lives inside `session.respond(to:)`. For one prompt the model may call several8/// tools, read what each one returned, and only then write its reply. We just watch it happen.9@MainActor10@Observable11final class TaskAgent {12    struct Message: Identifiable {13        enum Role { case user, agent, problem }14        let id = UUID()15        let role: Role16        let text: String17        var actions: [AgentAction] = []18    }19 20    let workspace: Workspace21    private(set) var messages: [Message] = []22    private(set) var isWorking = false23    private var firstActionOfTurn = 024    private var session: LanguageModelSession25 26    init(workspace: Workspace) {27        self.workspace = workspace28        session = Self.makeSession(for: workspace)29    }30 31    // MARK: - Session32 33    private static func makeSession(for workspace: Workspace) -> LanguageModelSession {34        let tools: [any Tool] = [35            AddTaskTool(workspace: workspace),36            CompleteTaskTool(workspace: workspace),37            PrioritizeTaskTool(workspace: workspace),38            SwitchLayoutTool(workspace: workspace),39        ]40        let titles = workspace.tasks.map(\.title).joined(separator: ", ")41        let instructions = """42        You are an agent inside a task-board app. You change the board ONLY by calling tools.43        - Call a tool for every change the user asks for. One request may need several tools.44        - To refer to a task, pass the user's own words for it.45        - Read every tool result. Only say something happened if a tool result says it did.46        - Reply in one short, friendly sentence.47        Tasks on the board when this conversation started: \(titles).48        """49        return LanguageModelSession(model: SystemLanguageModel.default, tools: tools, instructions: instructions)50    }51 52    /// Forgets the conversation. The board is not touched.53    func newConversation() {54        messages.removeAll()55        session = Self.makeSession(for: workspace)56    }57 58    /// Loads the model early so the first reply is faster.59    func prewarm() {60        if unavailableReason == nil { session.prewarm() }61    }62 63    // MARK: - Talking to the model64 65    /// What the tools have done so far in the current turn, shown live while the model works.66    var liveActions: [AgentAction] {67        isWorking ? Array(workspace.actions.dropFirst(firstActionOfTurn)) : []68    }69 70    func send(_ text: String) async {71        let prompt = text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)72        guard !prompt.isEmpty, !isWorking else { return }73        messages.append(Message(role: .user, text: prompt))74        firstActionOfTurn = workspace.actions.count75        isWorking = true76        defer { isWorking = false }77 78        // No Apple Intelligence (e.g. a simulator on a Mac without it)? Use the keyword stand-in.79        if unavailableReason != nil {80            let reply = await SimulatedAgent.respond(to: prompt, workspace: workspace)81            messages.append(Message(role: .agent, text: reply, actions: liveActions))82            return83        }84 85        do {86            let response = try await session.respond(to: prompt)87            messages.append(Message(role: .agent, text: response.content, actions: liveActions))⋯88        } catch let error as LanguageModelSession.GenerationError {89            var text = error.localizedDescription90            if case .exceededContextWindowSize = error {91                // The on-device model has a small context window. Start fresh and let the user retry.92                session = Self.makeSession(for: workspace)93                text = "This conversation got too long for the on-device model, so I started a fresh one. Please try again."94            }95            messages.append(Message(role: .problem, text: text, actions: liveActions))96        } catch {97            messages.append(Message(role: .problem, text: error.localizedDescription, actions: liveActions))98        }99    }100 101    // MARK: - Availability102 103    /// `nil` when Apple Intelligence is ready, otherwise what to tell the user.104    var unavailableReason: String? {105        switch SystemLanguageModel.default.availability {106        case .available:107            nil108        case .unavailable(.deviceNotEligible):109            "This device doesn’t support Apple Intelligence."110        case .unavailable(.appleIntelligenceNotEnabled):111            "Turn on Apple Intelligence in Settings to use the agent."112        case .unavailable(.modelNotReady):113            "Apple Intelligence is still downloading. Try again in a few minutes."114        case .unavailable:115            "Apple Intelligence isn’t available right now."116        }117    }118}

Your First Tool

Teach the agent something new: removing high priority from a task. You'll follow the same three steps every tool needs: a command, a tool, and registering it.

Download Project Files

Section 1

Add the Command

Start in Workspace, where every change lives. The command works for anyone; the agent's way in turns words into a task first.

  1. Step 1

    Add deprioritize(_:by:) next to prioritize, and deprioritizeTask(_:) next to prioritizeTask. Notice it says "Nothing changed." if the task isn't high priority.

    Workspace.swift
    ⋯1import Foundation2import Observation3 4/// Something the agent did, shown as a chip in the chat.5struct AgentAction: Identifiable, Hashable {6    let id = UUID()7    let symbol: String8    let summary: String9}10 11/// Who made a change: a tap in the UI, or a tool call by the agent.12enum ChangedBy {13    case user, agent14}15 16/// The app's state, and the only place it changes.17///18/// Every change is a "command" method. Taps in the UI and the agent's tools call the SAME methods,19/// only `by:` differs, so the AI can never do anything the user couldn't do. Each command returns20/// a short, truthful sentence: that sentence is what the model reads back after calling a tool.21@MainActor22@Observable23final class Workspace {24    var tasks: [TaskItem] = TaskItem.samples25    var layout: BoardLayout = .grid26    /// Everything the agent has done, in order.27    private(set) var actions: [AgentAction] = []28 29    /// Priority first, then to-do, then done.30    var orderedTasks: [TaskItem] {31        let open = tasks.filter { !$0.isDone }32        return open.filter(\.isHighPriority) + open.filter { !$0.isHighPriority } + tasks.filter(\.isDone)33    }34 35    // MARK: - Commands (shared by taps and tools)36 37    @discardableResult38    func addTask(title: String, category: TaskCategory, highPriority: Bool, by: ChangedBy) -> String {39        tasks.append(TaskItem(title: title, category: category, isHighPriority: highPriority))40        let detail = highPriority ? " (high priority)" : ""41        return record("plus.circle.fill", "Added “\(title)”\(detail)", by: by)42    }43 44    @discardableResult45    func complete(_ id: TaskItem.ID, by: ChangedBy) -> String {46        guard let index = index(of: id) else { return "That task no longer exists." }47        guard !tasks[index].isDone else { return "“\(tasks[index].title)” was already done. Nothing changed." }48        tasks[index].isDone = true49        tasks[index].revision += 150        return record("checkmark.circle.fill", "Completed “\(tasks[index].title)”", by: by)51    }52 53    @discardableResult54    func prioritize(_ id: TaskItem.ID, by: ChangedBy) -> String {55        guard let index = index(of: id) else { return "That task no longer exists." }56        guard !tasks[index].isHighPriority else { return "“\(tasks[index].title)” is already high priority. Nothing changed." }57        tasks[index].isHighPriority = true58        tasks[index].revision += 159        return record("star.fill", "Prioritised “\(tasks[index].title)”", by: by)60    }61 62    @discardableResult63    func deprioritize(_ id: TaskItem.ID, by: ChangedBy) -> String {64        guard let index = index(of: id) else { return "That task no longer exists." }65        guard tasks[index].isHighPriority else { return "“\(tasks[index].title)” isn’t high priority. Nothing changed." }66        tasks[index].isHighPriority = false67        tasks[index].revision += 168        return record("star.slash.fill", "Deprioritised “\(tasks[index].title)”", by: by)69    }70 71    @discardableResult72    func delete(_ id: TaskItem.ID, by: ChangedBy) -> String {73        guard let index = index(of: id) else { return "That task no longer exists." }74        let title = tasks.remove(at: index).title⋯75        return record("trash.fill", "Deleted “\(title)”", by: by)76    }77 78    @discardableResult79    func switchLayout(to newLayout: BoardLayout, by: ChangedBy) -> String {80        guard layout != newLayout else { return "The board is already in \(newLayout.rawValue) view. Nothing changed." }81        layout = newLayout82        return record("rectangle.3.group.fill", "Switched to \(newLayout.rawValue) view", by: by)83    }84 85    /// A tap on a tile: done ↔ open.86    func toggleDone(_ id: TaskItem.ID) {87        guard let index = index(of: id) else { return }88        tasks[index].isDone.toggle()89        tasks[index].revision += 190    }91 92    /// Puts the demo back to the start.93    func reset() {94        tasks = TaskItem.samples95        layout = .grid96        actions = []97    }98 99    // MARK: - The agent's way in: words → task → the same command100 101    func completeTask(_ query: String) -> String {102        guard let id = findTask(query) else { return problem(query) }103        return complete(id, by: .agent)104    }105 106    func prioritizeTask(_ query: String) -> String {107        guard let id = findTask(query) else { return problem(query) }108        return prioritize(id, by: .agent)109    }110 111    func deprioritizeTask(_ query: String) -> String {112        guard let id = findTask(query) else { return problem(query) }113        return deprioritize(id, by: .agent)114    }115 116    // MARK: - Helpers⋯117 118    /// Returns the summary as a sentence for the model. Agent changes are also logged as chat chips.119    func record(_ symbol: String, _ summary: String, by: ChangedBy) -> String {120        if by == .agent {121            actions.append(AgentAction(symbol: symbol, summary: summary))122        }123        return summary + "."124    }125 126    func index(of id: TaskItem.ID) -> Int? {127        tasks.firstIndex { $0.id == id }128    }129 130    /// Finds the one task the user means, e.g. "unit tests" → "Write Unit Test Suite".131    /// Returns nil when nothing matches or more than one task does.132    func findTask(_ query: String) -> TaskItem.ID? {133        let wanted = Self.words(in: query).filter { !["the", "a", "my", "task"].contains($0) }134        guard !wanted.isEmpty else { return nil }135        let matches = tasks.filter { task in136            let titleWords = Self.words(in: task.title)137            return wanted.allSatisfy { word in138                titleWords.contains { $0.hasPrefix(word) || (word.hasPrefix($0) && $0.count >= 4) }139            }140        }141        let open = matches.filter { !$0.isDone }142        let candidates = open.isEmpty ? matches : open143        return candidates.count == 1 ? candidates[0].id : nil144    }145 146    /// Tells the model honestly why nothing happened, so it can ask the user instead of pretending.147    func problem(_ query: String) -> String {148        actions.append(AgentAction(symbol: "questionmark.circle.fill", summary: "Couldn’t pick a task for “\(query)”"))149        let titles = tasks.filter { !$0.isDone }.map { "“\($0.title)”" }.joined(separator: ", ")150        return "No single task matches “\(query)”, so nothing changed. Open tasks: \(titles). Ask the user which one they mean."151    }152 153    private static func words(in text: String) -> [String] {154        text.lowercased().split { !$0.isLetter && !$0.isNumber }.map(String.init)155    }156}

Section 2

Write and Register the Tool

The tool is a thin adapter. Its description is what the model reads to decide when to use it.

  1. Step 1

    In Tools.swift, replace the lab comment with DeprioritizeTaskTool.

    Tools.swift
    ⋯1import FoundationModels2 3// The agent's four tools.4//5// A tool is a function the model may decide to call. You give it:6//   • a name and a description  → how the model knows WHEN to use it7//   • @Generable Arguments      → what the model must fill in (it can't invent other fields)8//   • call(arguments:)          → your Swift code, which returns what really happened9//10// Each tool here is a thin adapter over one Workspace command.11 12struct AddTaskTool: Tool {13    let name = "addTask"14    let description = "Adds a new task to the board."15    let workspace: Workspace16 17    @Generable18    struct Arguments {19        @Guide(description: "A short task title in Title Case, e.g. 'Review Pull Requests'")20        var title: String21        var category: TaskCategory22        @Guide(description: "True only if the user says the task is important, urgent or high priority")23        var highPriority: Bool24    }25 26    func call(arguments: Arguments) async throws -> String {27        await workspace.addTask(title: arguments.title, category: arguments.category, highPriority: arguments.highPriority, by: .agent)28    }29}30 31struct CompleteTaskTool: Tool {32    let name = "completeTask"33    let description = "Marks an existing task as done."34    let workspace: Workspace35 36    @Generable37    struct Arguments {38        @Guide(description: "The user's words for the task, e.g. 'unit tests'")39        var task: String40    }41 42    func call(arguments: Arguments) async throws -> String {43        await workspace.completeTask(arguments.task)44    }45}46 47struct PrioritizeTaskTool: Tool {48    let name = "prioritizeTask"49    let description = "Marks an existing task as high priority so it moves to the top."50    let workspace: Workspace51 52    @Generable53    struct Arguments {54        @Guide(description: "The user's words for the task, e.g. 'memory leak'")55        var task: String56    }57 58    func call(arguments: Arguments) async throws -> String {59        await workspace.prioritizeTask(arguments.task)60    }61}62 63struct SwitchLayoutTool: Tool {64    let name = "switchLayout"65    let description = "Changes how the board looks: grid of tiles, list of rows, or board with Priority / To Do / Done columns."66    let workspace: Workspace67 68    @Generable69    struct Arguments {70        var layout: BoardLayout71    }72 73    func call(arguments: Arguments) async throws -> String {74        await workspace.switchLayout(to: arguments.layout, by: .agent)75    }76}77 78struct DeprioritizeTaskTool: Tool {79    let name = "deprioritizeTask"80    let description = "Removes high priority from an   2. Step 2

    Register the tool in makeSession(for:). Run the app and say "The memory leak can wait." Then try vaguer wording, and see whether the model still picks your tool.

    TaskAgent.swift
    ⋯1import Foundation2import FoundationModels3import Observation4 5/// The agent: one on-device `LanguageModelSession` that holds the conversation and the tools.6///7/// The agentic loop lives inside `session.respond(to:)`. For one prompt the model may call several8/// tools, read what each one returned, and only then write its reply. We just watch it happen.9@MainActor10@Observable11final class TaskAgent {12    struct Message: Identifiable {13        enum Role { case user, agent, problem }14        let id = UUID()15        let role: Role16        let text: String17        var actions: [AgentAction] = []18    }19 20    let workspace: Workspace21    private(set) var messages: [Message] = []22    private(set) var isWorking = false23    private var firstActionOfTurn = 024    private var session: LanguageModelSession25 26    init(workspace: Workspace) {27        self.workspace = workspace28        session = Self.makeSession(for: workspace)29    }30 31    // MARK: - Session32 33    private static func makeSession(for workspace: Workspace) -> LanguageModelSession {34        let tools: [any Tool] = [35            AddTaskTool(workspace: workspace),36            CompleteTaskTool(workspace: workspace),37            PrioritizeTaskTool(workspace: workspace),38            SwitchLayoutTool(workspace: workspace),39            DeprioritizeTaskTool(workspace: workspace),40        ]41        let titles = workspace.tasks.map(\.title).joined(separator: ", ")42        let instructions = """⋯43        You are an agent inside a task-board app. You change the board ONLY by calling tools.44        - Call a tool for every change the user asks for. One request may need several tools.45        - To refer to a task, pass the user's own words for it.46        - Read every tool result. Only say something happened if a tool result says it did.47        - Reply in one short, friendly sentence.48        Tasks on the board when this conversation started: \(titles).49        """50        return LanguageModelSession(model: SystemLanguageModel.default, tools: tools, instructions: instructions)51    }52 53    /// Forgets the conversation. The board is not touched.54    func newConversation() {55        messages.removeAll()56        session = Self.makeSession(for: workspace)57    }58 59    /// Loads the model early so the first reply is faster.60    func prewarm() {61        if unavailableReason == nil { session.prewarm() }62    }63 64    // MARK: - Talking to the model65 66    /// What the tools have done so far in the current turn, shown live while the model works.67    var liveActions: [AgentAction] {68        isWorking ? Array(workspace.actions.dropFirst(firstActionOfTurn)) : []69    }70 71    func send(_ text: String) async {72        let prompt = text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)73        guard !prompt.isEmpty, !isWorking else { return }74        messages.append(Message(role: .user, text: prompt))75        firstActionOfTurn = workspace.actions.count76        isWorking = true77        defer { isWorking = false }78 79        // No Apple Intelligence (e.g. a simulator on a Mac without it)? Use the keyword stand-in.80        if unavailableReason != nil {81            let reply = await SimulatedAgent.respond(to: prompt, workspace: workspace)82            messages.append(Message(role: .agent, text: reply, actions: liveActions))83            return84        }85 86        do {87            let response = try await session.respond(to: prompt)88            messages.append(Message(role: .agent, text: response.content, actions: liveActions))89        } catch let error as LanguageModelSession.GenerationError {90            var text = error.localizedDescription91            if case .exceededContextWindowSize = error {92                // The on-device model has a small context window. Start fresh and let the user retry.93                session = Self.makeSession(for: workspace)94                text = "This conversation got too long for the on-device model, so I started a fresh one. Please try again."95            }96            messages.append(Message(role: .problem, text: text, actions: liveActions))97        } catch {98            messages.append(Message(role: .problem, text: error.localizedDescription, actions: liveActions))99        }100    }101 102    // MARK: - Availability103 104    /// `nil` when Apple Intelligence is ready, otherwise what to tell the user.105    var unavailableReason: String? {106        switch SystemLanguageModel.default.availability {107        case .available:108            nil109        case .unavailable(.deviceNotEligible):110            "This device doesn’t support Apple Intelligence."111        case .unavailable(.appleIntelligenceNotEnabled):112            "Turn on Apple Intelligence in Settings to use the agent."113        case .unavailable(.modelNotReady):114            "Apple Intelligence is still downloading. Try again in a few minutes."115        case .unavailable:116            "Apple Intelligence isn’t available right now."117        }118    }119}

Section 3

Give the User the Same Power

Anything the agent can do, the user should be able to do too.

  1. Step 1

    Add a Deprioritise item to the tile's context menu, calling deprioritize(task.id, by: .user). New tools need the real model: the simulated agent only knows the four built-in ones.
